How we'd take you to market

Four moves, in this order

Tap each one to see what it is and why it fits.

Fix what AI and Google read first

What
A fast phone site, a main heading and image descriptions on every buyer page, and product and Q&A markup that AI can quote.
Why
The home page scores 6 out of 100 for speed on a phone and takes 7.6 s to show its main image (run the Google test ↗). Eight page types have no main heading (the scan ↗).
Also
Google, Apple Maps and Bing listings, with one clear story: designed in New Zealand, ships to Australia.

Answer her questions in her words

What
A page, a short film, a post and a profile update for each question, linked together. We call each set a lever.
Order
Leaking on double unders first, then back to running after a baby, then training through perimenopause.
Proof
The first lever is already built. You can watch its film just below.

Get into the lists AI reads

What
We pitch the editors, reviewers and directories that AI leans on, in each market.
Why
Double Undies is missing from all six "best leakproof" roundups we read: Marie Claire ↗, Everyday Undies ↗, Trusted Consumers Reviews ↗, The Wearify ↗, Ever Leakproof ↗, Your Wear Guide ↗.

Re-ask the same questions monthly

What
Each month we ask AI the same 96 questions in New Zealand, Australia, the US and the UK.
Why
You see the count move from 6 and 20, and we see which lever earned it (how we measured ↗).
